key_insight: The paper introduces physics-augmented neural networks that learn uncertainty-aware hyperelastic constitutive laws as lower, mean, upper, and fuzzy response bounds while enforcing mechanics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This gives solid mechanics simulations a compact, distribution-free way to quantify aleatoric uncertainty in stress-strain behavior and propagate it into finite element analyses.
method: iPANN learns sparse lower, mean, and upper free-energy branches; stresses are obtained by automatic differentiation to bound noisy observations.
fPANN converts the interval model into a fuzzy-set representation using alpha-cut interpolation for nested admissible responses.
A two-stage transfer-learning strategy first fits a sparse mean model, then fine-tunes bound branches with smoothed L0 regularization and mechanistic constraints.
evidence_signal: The models were tested on synthetic isotropic hyperelastic data with heteroscedastic noise, shifted noise means, and varying noise magnitudes, and the learned bounds enclosed noisy stress data while generalizing to the test set.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on constrained training and sparse branch fitting, performance and interpretability may be sensitive to the quality of the initial mean model and to hyperparameter choices.
paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
